chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Be good in the vicinity of the Bounty.' I said, 'And what is being good in the vicinity of the Bounty?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The gratefulness to the one who has favoured (you) with it, and fulfilments of its rights.'

key_terms.النِّعَم: the bounties or blessings (plural of ni'mah)
key_terms.جِوَار: vicinity or proximity; here used metaphorically for treating or managing

ai.seo_question: How does Shia tradition define the proper way to treat divine blessings?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the concept of 'goodness in the vicinity of bounties' (husn al-jawar) by defining it as dual-dimensional gratitude: spiritual thanksgiving to the Giver and the practical fulfillment of each blessing's specific rights (huquq). This teaching underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis that divine favors are not merely possessions but trusts requiring active stewardship, linking material well-being to spiritual accountability. It reflects the broader theological principle that true appreciation of God’s grace is demonstrated through both verbal praise and the correct application of the blessing in accordance with its purpose.
